Challenge: Quantum Machine Learning (QML) promises exponential advantages for high-complexity data, yet four fundamental barriers prevent practical deployment: (1) scalability —NISQ devices cannot process high-dimensional scientific data; (2) trainability —gradient-based methods suffer barren plateaus, while gradient-free alternatives converge slowly with high sampling overhead, and expressive circuits often remain classically simulable; (3) temporal expressibility —existing QML architectures lack mechanisms for long-range sequence modeling; (4) reliability —no certification standards exist for QML robustness against adversarial attacks or hardware noise. Innovation: We pioneer four fundamental breakthroughs: (1) Improved Scalability via Multi-Chip Ensembles —partitioning high-dimensional data across independent QPUs with selective quantum connections; (2) Enhanced Trainability via Quantum Forward-Forward with Hybrid Quantum Genetic Algorithms —combining local "goodness" objectives with quantum evolutionary search to train deep, non-simulable circuits without gradients; (3) Temporal Expressibility via Quantum State Space Models with three-branch quantum superposition; (4) Reliability via Fuzzy Quantum Diffusion —exploiting physical quantum noise as a generative resource for hardware-native generative modeling. Enhanced Validation Strategy: Rather than claiming immediate quantum supremacy, we establish validated theoretical frameworks through staged validation with rigorous classical baselines ensuring objective quantum advantage assessment. Consortium: Our international partnership combines Seoul National University's multi-chip ensemble expertise, University of Naples' quantum computational intelligence leadership, Fraunhofer IKS's reliability and robustness standards, and Yonsei University's CERN collaboration experience. Expected Impact: This project transforms QML from experimental demonstrations to preliminary engineering validation, establishing Europe-Asia leadership in practical quantum machine learning while training the next generation of quantum algorithm engineers for industry deployment. Relevance to the topic addressed in the call : Novel quantum algorithms and software stacks: Four algorithms—Multi-Chip Ensembles, Quantum Forward-Forward with Hybrid Quantum Genetic Algorithms (QFF-HQGA), Quantum State Space Model (Q-SSM), Fuzzy-Quantum Diffusion—target scalability, trainability, temporal expressibility, and reliability bottlenecks, integrated into an open-source library. New architectures and programming paradigms, including hybrid approaches: Multi-Chip Ensembles introduce distributed quantum computing via QPU aggregation. All innovations are hybrid quantum-classical architectures optimized for NISQ constraints. Development of noisy intermediate-scale quantum platforms: Fuzzy-Quantum Diffusion exploits noise as a generative resource. The QML Reliability Certification Standard provides the first formal robustness metrics. Resource theory for quantum information: We establish the first resource theory for distributed QML, proving ensemble aggregation achieves collective advantage while Selective Entanglement optimizes expressivity-trainability trade-offs. Superposition, interference, and entanglement for enhanced functionalities: Q-SSM uses three-branch superposition for interference-like features; Multi-Chip Ensembles leverage restricted entanglement to prevent barren plateaus; QFF-HQGA employs entangled crossover for evolutionary optimization. Understanding and control of open quantum systems: Fuzzy-Quantum Diffusion models decoherence as continuous uncertainty via POVMs, converting noise into a computational resource. 1. Excellence (max. 6 pages) 1.1 Targeted Breakthrough, Baseline of Knowledge and Skills Targeted Breakthroughs This project targets four fundamental barriers preventing Quantum Machine Learning (QML) from achieving practical advantage. Current QML remains confined to small-scale demonstrations reliant on heuristic ansatzes that become untrainable at scale. We shift the paradigm from "heuristic QML" to "Physics-Aware & Scalable QML" —algorithms designed for NISQ constraints with rigorous theoretical foundations and practical validation pathways . Breakthrough 1 – Scalability via Multi-Chip Ensembles: We partition high-dimensional data across k independent QPUs, each processing locally-correlated inputs [1] . Selective Entanglement introduces inter-chip quantum connections only for globally-dependent features. Classical aggregation provides algorithmic error mitigation: independent chip errors average out (variance reduction ∝ 1/k) without resource-heavy correction codes, establishing a resource theory for "Collective Quantum Advantage" . This architecture aligns with emerging modular quantum hardware platforms (e.g., IBM Quantum, IonQ, Pasqal), enabling direct deployment as interconnected QPU systems become available. Breakthrough 2 – Trainability via Quantum Forward-Forward & Hybrid Quantum Genetic Algorithm: We integrate Quantum Forward-Forward (QFF) [2] with Hybrid Quantum Genetic Algorithm (HQGA) [3] . QFF decomposes deep circuits into layers optimizing local goodness objectives, mathematically circumventing barren plateaus [4] while preserving expressivity. Hybrid Quantum Genetic Algorithm encodes parameters as quantum chromosomes —superpositions enabling parallel fitness evaluation—using entangled crossover and quantum elitism . Breakthrough 3 – Temporal Expressibility via Q-SSM: We develop Quantum State Space Models (Q-SSM) [5] integrating three-branch quantum superposition with LSTM-style gating. Quantum circuits access 2ⁿ-dimensional Hilbert space with O(n×l) parameters versus O(N²) classically. The architecture achieves O(L) complexity through chunked processing, matching classical state space models [6], [7] efficiency while exploiting quantum feature expressivity. Breakthrough 4 – Reliability via Fuzzy Quantum Diffusion: We exploit physical quantum noise as a generative resource [8], [9] . Fuzzy Quantum Logic via Positive Operator-Valued Measures [10] provides continuous measurements, enabling Hardware-Attention U-Net to learn device-specific noise fingerprints. To curb uncertainty from noisy models further, we design robustness and safety certification [11], [12] that meet industrial-grade robustness [13] standards, with verified resilience to targeted attacks and untargeted perturbations. Rather than waiting for fault tolerance, we redesign algorithms to exploit these constraints. Core hypothesis: Quantum advantage lies in feature representation (Hilbert space expressivity with parameter efficiency), not error-free computation. Our hybrid architectures extract quantum features via shallow, noise-resilient circuits while delegating temporal memory and output generation to classical components proven effective for these tasks. Relevant Achievements: ● Definition of Quantum Fuzzy Logic frameworks for uncertainty management using POVMs. ● Development of Hybrid Quantum Genetic Algorithms (HQGA) with entangled crossover and quantum elitism for optimizing Variational Quantum Circuits. ● Application of Quantum Forward-Forward (QFF) algorithms with local "goodness" objectives to prevent Barren Plateaus in QML. ● Hardware validation of quantum fuzzy inference engines on both superconducting and ion-trap backends, demonstrating real-world implementability (IEEE TQE, 2024). ● Analysis of quantum noise effects on evolutionary algorithms , providing theoretical grounding for the noise-as-resource paradigm. Role in project: Optimization & Intelligence Lead Naples leads WP3 (Physics-Informed Optimization & Generative Models) . They provide the QFF-HQGA algorithms to drive gradient-free training, design the Fuzzy Logic Controllers for the Fuzzy-Quantum Diffusion models using POVMs, and develop Hardware-Attention U-Net architectures for noise-resilient generative modeling. Prof. Acampora's EVOVAQ framework provides the software infrastructure for WP2 (Scalable Distributed Quantum Architectures) , while his D-NISQ expertise validates the divide-and-conquer approach. Naples also supports WP4 (Neuro Validation) through QFF-HQGA driven brain connectivity optimization, and WP5 in adversarial evolutionary testing. This project addresses two sensitive domains through a "Safety-by-Design" framework overseen by the Innovation & Ethics Board (Lead: Fraunhofer IKS): ● Human Biological Data (Neuroscience): WP4 processes EEG/fMRI data, raising privacy and bias risks. ○ Legal Compliance: We strictly adhere to GDPR (EU) and PIPA (South Korea). SNU pseudonymizes all clinical data at the source before consortium sharing. ○ Technical Mitigation: A core objective is developing Fuzzy-Quantum Diffusion (WP3) to generate high-fidelity synthetic datasets. This minimizes the exposure of real patient data while maintaining statistical validity. ○ Bias Mitigation: To prevent algorithmic discrimination in brain signal analysis, we implement gender-stratified validation (balanced 50/50 male/female training data) as defined in Section 1.5. ● Dual-Use Potential (Cybersecurity): WP5 develops adversarial attack protocols to stress-test QML models. ○ Responsible Disclosure: We adopt an "As Closed As Necessary" policy. Detailed attack vectors are encrypted and restricted to the consortium. Public dissemination is limited to the Defense/Certification Standards rather than offensive tools. Justification of Methodology. The use of high-dimensional human data is scientifically unavoidable to validate the Temporal Expressibility of Q-SSM (Objective 3) ; synthetic toy datasets fail to capture the long-range correlations required to prove quantum advantage. Similarly, developing rigorous adversarial attacks is the only mathematical method to certify Lipschitz bounds (Objective 4) , converting experimental QML into safe, industrial-grade technology. 5.
